title: A finite normal integral cover is the normalization in its function field
statement: Let $X,Z$ be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], with $Z$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and normal, meaning every local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain. Let $f:Z\to X$ be finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Put $F=k(X)$ and $L=k(Z)$ [def-sc-function-field], and suppose the induced field extension $L/F$ is finite [def-pc-field-extension]. For every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, write $f^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The structural map $A\to B$ is injective. Under the germ embedding $B\subseteq L=\operatorname{Frac}B$, the ring $B$ is exactly the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The corresponding affine identifications agree after restriction to principal opens and on overlaps; they give a canonical $X$-isomorphism $Z\cong X^L$, where $X^L$ is the normalization of $X$ in $L$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Its restriction to the generic point is the identity on $L$, and it is uniquely determined by being over $X$ and inducing this identity. Neither normality of $X$ nor etaleness of $f$ is required.

source.place: Tag 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), applied to the generic-point map and a finite normal integral cover; Properties Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections) and Algebra Tag 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral). Affine integral-closure argument of returned steps 6--7.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$. Finiteness gives $f^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite as an $A$-module. Surjectivity makes this open nonempty. Both opens are integral since nonempty affine opens of integral schemes have domain coordinate rings. The affine-function-field lemma identifies their germ embeddings with $A\subset F$ and $B\subset L=\operatorname{Frac}B$. The surjective map $f$ is dominant, and its generic stalk map $F\to L$ is the function-field map: it sends the germ of $a\in A$ to the germ of its pullback in $B$. A unital homomorphism of fields is injective, so if $a$ pulls back to zero in $B$, its image in $F$ is zero and hence $a=0$. Thus $A\to B$ is injective, with all embeddings compatible inside $L$.

proof.text: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$, the affine stalk-localization statement identifies $B_{\mathfrak m}$ with the corresponding local ring of $Z$. That local ring is an integrally closed domain by hypothesis. Transport normal-domain structure across the stalk isomorphism, and apply normality local at maximal ideals to the domain $B$. It follows that $B$ is integrally closed in its fraction field $L$. This uses neither normality of $A$ nor Noetherianity of $A$.

source.place: Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections), affine case; schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)(6); algebra.tex Tag 030B (lemma-normality-is-local)

proof.text: Put $C=\overline A^{\,L}$, the subring of elements of $L$ integral over $A$. Every $b\in B$ is integral over $A$ by finite-algebra integrality. Its monic equation remains an equation after the germ embedding $B\hookrightarrow L$. Consequently $B\subseteq C$ as subrings of $L$.

Conversely let $c\in C$. Choose a monic equation $c^n+\sum_{i<n}a_ic^i=0$ with $a_i\in A$. Regard each $a_i$ in $B$ through $A\hookrightarrow B$. This same equation makes $c\in L$ integral over $B$. Since step 2 proved $B$ integrally closed in $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$, we have $c\in B$. Thus $C=B$ inside $L$. By the affine description of normalization in a finite function-field extension and contravariance of spectrum, the identity of this subring gives an isomorphism $e_V:f^{-1}V\xrightarrow{\sim}(X^L)|_V$ over $V$. Its generic field map is the identity on $L$, because the ring map on $C=B$ is the identity and every element of $L$ is a fraction of elements of $B$.

source.place: Tag 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), affine integral-closure argument; properties.tex Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections)

proof.text: For $a\in A$ nonzero, the inverse image of $D(a)\subset V$ is $D(f^\sharp a)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$: a prime belongs to the inverse image exactly when it does not contain $f^\sharp a$. The principal-open section formulas give $A_a$ and $B_a$, with restriction $b\mapsto b/1$. Integral closure commuting with localization identifies $\overline{A_a}^{\,L}$ with $C_a$, since localization of $L$ at the nonzero image of $a$ is $L$ itself. Localizing $B=C\subset L$ gives the identity $B_a=C_a\subset L$. Hence the restriction of $e_V$ is exactly $e_{D(a)}$, including its map on sections. For $a=0$ both opens are empty and compatibility is automatic.

These local maps agree on arbitrary overlaps as well. Cover $V\cap V'$ by affine opens $W$; no affineness of $V\cap V'$ is assumed. For nested nonempty affine opens $W\subset V$, both source restriction and normalization restriction, after their germ embeddings, send each section to the same element of $L$. For the source this is the definition of restriction and germ; for normalization it is its construction from the integral-closure subrings in $L$, with the principal transitions verified in step 5. The injective germ embedding on $f^{-1}W$ therefore makes the restriction square with the identity $C_V=B_V$ and $C_W=B_W$ commute. The same applies with $V'$ in place of $V$. Thus both restricted maps equal $e_W$, so they agree on the overlap by morphism gluing. Glue the $e_V$ and, separately, their inverse maps. The two composites are identity on each chart, hence globally identity by uniqueness in morphism gluing. This gives the canonical $X$-isomorphism $e:Z\cong X^L$, inducing the identity on $L$.

source.place: Tag 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), affine construction; schemes.tex Tag 01JA (section-glueing-schemes), gluing local morphisms

proof.text: Finally let $u:Z\to X^L$ be another morphism over $X$ inducing the identity on $L$. On each nonempty affine $V\subset X$ it restricts to a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ and hence a ring map $u_V^\sharp:C\to B$. For $c\in C$, its image under $u_V^\sharp$ has germ $c\in L$, by the stipulated generic identity. Since $B\hookrightarrow L$ is injective, $u_V^\sharp(c)=c$. The affine spectrum correspondence gives $u|_{f^{-1}V}=e_V$, and uniqueness in morphism gluing gives $u=e$. In particular the asserted isomorphism is uniquely determined. The proof nowhere assumes etaleness of $f$ or normality of $X$.
